subcompetencies.name: Evaluation and Diagnosis of the Patient with Addiction or Co-Occurring Disorders

level_1: Performs biopsychosocial history and targeted examination, including assessment for patient safety and risk of self and other harm, intoxication, and overdose
Incorporates collateral information, other assessments, subtle findings, and conflicting information into a complete differential diagnosis
level_2: Organizes, summarizes information, and develops a differential diagnosis
Performs comprehensive patient evaluation, including patients with complex presentations
level_3: Incorporates biopsychosocial history, examination, lab, and collateral data into patient evaluation
Uses all available information to generate a complete and accurate differential diagnosis; takes steps to resolve apparent inconsistencies, and continuously reassesses the diagnosis
level_4: Organizes and accurately summarizes information, and develops a differential diagnosis while avoiding premature closure
Provides a significant contribution in education or scholarly work in the evaluation of patients with substance use and addictive disorders (e.g., teaches a course, research, publication)
level_5: Performs comprehensive patient evaluation of routine patient presentation, including interpretation of toxicology testing
Provides a significant contribution in education or scholarly work in differential diagnosis and diagnostic criteria

subcompetencies.name: Psychotherapy, Behavioral, and Psychosocial Interventions in Substance Use and Addictive Disorders

level_1: Establishes and maintains a therapeutic alliance and provides appropriate psychotherapy
Incorporates co- occurring medical and psychiatric disorders into a comprehensive individualized treatment plan
level_2: Sets treatment goals in collaboration with the patient, including community resources
Delivers various types of evidence-based psychotherapy
level_3: Uses current practice guidelines in evaluation and psychotherapeutic treatment
Develops comprehensive, individualized treatment plans for patients with complex presentations
level_4: Develops comprehensive, individualized treatment plans with patients to treat uncomplicated substance use and addictive disorders
Competently teaches at least one evidence- based psychotherapy to other learners or contributes to scholarly work in psychotherapy for substance use and addictive disorders
level_5: Participates in the delivery of evidence- based psychotherapy

subcompetencies.name: Pharmacological Interventions for Substance Use and Addictive Disorders

level_1: Appropriately prescribes commonly used psychopharmacologic agents and recognizes patients with acute intoxication or withdrawal
Incorporates co- occurring medical and psychiatric disorders into a comprehensive individualized treatment plan, including psychopharmacology
level_2: Sets treatment goals in collaboration with the patient, including general indications, dosing parameters, and common side effects for prescribed psychopharmacologic agents
Titrates dosages; manages side effects and complex drug interactions for patients prescribed multiple medications; and manages complex intoxication, withdrawal, and long-term management
level_3: Appropriately prescribes pharmacologic agents for substance use and addictive disorders, including for the management of intoxication and withdrawal states
Develops comprehensive, individualized treatment plans, including psychopharmacology, for patients with complex presentations
level_4: Develops comprehensive, individualized treatment plans, including psychopharmacology, for patients with uncomplicated substance use and addictive disorders
Contributes significantly to education or scholarly work in psychopharmacology for substance use and addictive disorders
level_5: Manages pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic drug interactions for patients prescribed multiple medications and/or using non-prescribed substances

subcompetencies.name: Clinical Neuroscience of Substance Use and Addictive Disorders

level_1: Describes neurobiological and genetic hypotheses of common psychiatric disorders
Describes the neuropharmacology and mechanisms of action of agents used for treatment of addictive disorders
Teaches others about the neuropharmacology of addictive substances
level_2: Describes the categories of common and uncommon addictive substances
Describes the basic and neurophysiology related to the pathophysiology of addictive disorders
Integrates knowledge of neuropharmacology into selection of appropriate agents for patients
level_3: Describes the general indications and common side effects for commonly prescribed psychopharmacologic agents for addictive disorders
Describes the detailed neuropharmacology of all classes of addictive substances, including emerging addictive substances
Designs a neuroscience course focusing on substance use and addictive disorders
level_4: Describes the basic neuroanatomy of addictive disorders
Demonstrates understanding of the detailed mechanisms of action and side effects of pharmacologic agents for addictive disorders, including the potential for medication interactions
Participates in a scholarly activity related to the neuroscience or neuropharmacology of addiction
level_5: Demonstrates knowledge of the basic principles of the neuropharmacology of common addictive substances
Incorporates the latest research findings into discussions of the neuroscience of addictive disorders

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of risk factors that contribute to the development of substance use and addictive disorders
Describes the medical effects of addictive substances and psychiatric comorbidity
Applies current practice guidelines for the treatment of substance use and addictive disorders
level_2: Describes appropriate criteria to determine the necessary level of care for patients
Describes the developmental trajectories of substance use and addictive disorders
Demonstrates advanced knowledge sufficient to treat patients with complex medical, psychiatric, and addictive co-occurring disorders
level_3: Demonstrates sufficient knowledge to perform initial evaluations of patients with medical, psychiatric, and substance use and addictive disorders
Consistently applies appropriate criteria to determine necessary level of care for patients
Teaches others about or engages in research on biological, environmental, social, and psychological factors that contribute to the development of substance use and addictive disorders
level_4: Describes biological, social, psychological, and epidemiological factors that contribute to or protect against the development of substance use and addictive disorders
Applies knowledge of addictive and co- occurring conditions in patients with medical and psychiatric disorders
Teaches others about or engages in research related to level of care and treatment guidelines
level_5: Incorporates risk of morbidity and mortality from substance use in describing the appropriate level of care for patients
Applies knowledge of the biological, environmental, social, psychological, and epidemiological factors that contribute to the development of substance use and addictive disorders
Teaches others about or engages in research related to the interface of medical, psychiatric, and substance use and addictive disorders

subcompetencies.name: Psychotherapy, Behavioral, and Psychosocial Treatments, including Individual Therapies, Group

level_1: Lists the currently available non- pharmacologic treatment modalities for substance use and addictive disorders
level_2: Describes basic theoretical principles, components, and techniques for the use of several non- pharmacologic treatments for substance use and addictive disorders
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of the evidence base for non- pharmacological treatments for substance use and addictive disorders
level_4: Demonstrates comprehensive knowledge of the current evidence for non- pharmacological treatments for substance use and addictive disorders
level_5: Teaches others or engages in research on the delivery of non- pharmacological treatments for substance use and addictive disorders

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of common patient safety events
Describes local quality improvement initiatives (e.g., reduced infection rates, overdose rates, suicide rates; increased access to evidence- based treatment)
Discloses patient safety events to patients and patients’ families (simulated or actual)
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of how to report patient safety events
Participates in analysis of patient safety events (simulated or actual)
Demonstrates the skills required to identify, develop, implement, and analyze a quality improvement project
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of basic quality improvement methodologies and metrics
Participates in disclosure of patient safety events to patients and patients’ families (simulated or actual)
Actively engages teams and processes to improve systems to prevent patient safety events
level_4: Identifies system factors that lead to patient safety events
Participates in local quality improvement initiatives
Models or mentors others in the disclosure of patient safety events
level_5: Reports patient safety events through institutional reporting systems (simulated or actual)
Conducts analysis of patient safety events and offers error prevention strategies (simulated or actual)
Creates, implements, and assesses quality improvement initiatives at the institutional or community level

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of care coordination
Identifies specific population and community health needs for the local population
Role models and serves as a patient advocate for safe and effective transitions of care/hand- offs within and across health care delivery systems, including outpatient settings
level_2: Identifies key elements for safe and effective transitions of care and hand-offs
Coordinates care of patients in complex clinical situations effectively using the roles of the interprofessional teams
Participates in changing and adapting practice to provide for the needs of specific populations
level_3: Demonstrates awareness of population and community health needs
Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in complex clinical situations
Analyzes the process of care coordination and leads in the design and implementation of improvements
level_4: Coordinates care of patients in routine clinical situations effectively using the roles of the interprofessional teams
Uses local resources effectively to meet the needs of a patient population and community
Improves quality of transitions of care within and across health care delivery systems to optimize patient outcomes
level_5: Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in routine clinical situations
Role models effective coordination of patient- centered care among different disciplines and specialties
Leads innovations and advocates for populations and communities with health care needs

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Identifies key components of the complex health care system
Demonstrates use of information technology and documentation required for medical practice
Advocates for patient care needs, including mobilizing community resources
level_2: Describes practice models and basic addiction care payment systems
Discusses how individual practice affects the broader system
Analyzes individual practice patterns and professional requirements in preparation for practice
level_3: Identifies basic knowledge domains for effective transition to practice
Engages with patients in shared decision making and advocates for appropriate care and parity
Advocates for or leads systems change that enhances high-value, efficient, and effective patient care and transitions of care
level_4: Describes how components of a complex health care system are interrelated, and how this impacts patient care
Describes core administrative knowledge needed for transition to practice
Participates in advocacy activities for access to care in addiction treatment and reimbursement
level_5: Identifies barriers to care in different health care systems
Manages various components of the complex health care system to provide high- value, efficient, and effective patient care and transitions of care
Educates others to prepare them to transition to practice

level_1: Demonstrates how to access and summarize available evidence, and incorporate patient preferences and values, to the care of a routine patient
level_2: Articulates clinical questions and elicits patient preferences and values to guide evidence-based care
level_3: Locates and applies the best available evidence, integrated with patient preference, to the care of complex patients
level_4: Critically appraises conflicting evidence and applies it to guide the care of an individual patient
level_5: Mentors others to critically appraise and apply evidence for complex patients, and/or participates in the development of guidelines

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth

level_1: Accepts responsibility for personal and professional development by establishing goals
Designs and implements a learning plan, with supervision
Challenges assumptions and considers alternatives in narrowing the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
level_2: Identifies the factors that contribute to gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Seeks performance data episodically
Uses performance data to measure the effectiveness of the learning plan, and, when necessary, improves it
level_3: Recognizes opportunities to improve performance
Analyzes, reflects on, and institutes behavioral change(s) to narrow the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Models consistently seeking performance data
level_4: Demonstrates openness to performance data (feedback and other input) to inform goals
Independently creates and implements a learning plan
Mentors others on reflective practice
level_5: Analyzes and reflects on the factors that contribute to gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Seeks performance data consistently
Facilitates the design and implementation of learning plans for others

level_1: Identifies and describes core professional behavior
Analyzes straightforward situations using ethical principles
Responds appropriately to professionalism lapses of colleagues
level_2: Recognizes that one’s behavior in professional settings affects others
Demonstrates professional behavior in complex or stressful situations
Recognizes and uses appropriate resources for managing and resolving ethical dilemmas as needed (e.g., ethics consultations, literature review, risk management/legal consultation)
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of core ethical principles
Describes when and how to appropriately report professionalism lapses in others, including strategies for addressing common barriers to reporting
Models professional behavior and ethical principles
level_4: Demonstrates professional behavior in routine situations
Analyzes complex situations using ethical principles and recognizes when help is needed
Seeks to address issues of lapses in professionalism on a systems level
level_5: Takes responsibility for one’s own professionalism lapses and responds appropriately
Recognizes situations that may trigger professionalism lapses and intervenes to prevent lapses in oneself and others
Identifies and seeks to address system-level factors that induce or exacerbate ethical problems or impede their resolution

level_1: Completes tasks and responsibilities
Is recognized by oneself, the patient, the patient’s family, and medical staff members as the patient’s primary psychiatric addiction care physician
level_2: Introduces oneself as the patient’s fellow physician
Recognizes when others are unable to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner and assists in problem solving
level_3: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in routine situations; identifies potential contributing factors for lapses; describes strategies for ensuring timely task completion in the future
Displays increasing autonomy and leadership in ensuring patients receive the best possible care
level_4: Accepts the role of the patient’s physician and takes responsibility (under supervision) for ensuring that the patient receives the best possible care
Provides innovative ideas/plans for improvements to system outcomes
level_5: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in complex or stressful situations
Serves as a role model in demonstrating responsibility for ensuring that patients receive the best possible care

level_1: Recognizes the importance of addressing personal and professional well-being
Independently develops a plan to promote personal and professional well-being
level_2: Lists available resources for personal and professional well-being
Describes institutional programs designed to examine systemic contributors to burnout
level_3: Describes institutional resources designed to promote well-being
Creates institutional level interventions that promote colleagues’ well-being
level_4: With assistance, proposes a plan to promote personal and professional well-being
Contributes to institutional programs designed to examine systemic contributors to burnout, or participates in research in this area
level_5: Recognizes which institutional factors positively or negatively affect well-being

level_1: Uses language and non- verbal communication to demonstrate empathic curiosity and respect, and establish rapport
Organizes and initiates communication with the patient/patient’s family by introducing stakeholders, setting the agenda, clarifying expectations, and verifying understanding of the clinical situation
Independently recognizes biases and attempts to proactively minimize their contribution to communication barriers
level_2: Identifies common barriers to effective communication
Establishes a therapeutic relationship in challenging patient encounters; uses non- verbal communication skills effectively
Independently uses shared decision making to align the patient’s/patient’s family’s values, goals, and preferences with treatment options to make a personalized care plan
level_3: Recognizes communication strategies may need to be adjusted based on clinical context
When prompted, reflects on biases that may contribute to communication barriers
Mentors others in situational awareness and critical self-reflection to consistently develop positive therapeutic relationships
level_4: Establishes a therapeutic relationship in straightforward encounters using active listening and clear language
With guidance, sensitively and compassionately delivers medical information, elicits the patient’s/patient’s family’s values, goals, and preferences; acknowledges uncertainty and conflict
Models self-awareness practice while identifying and teaching a contextual approach to minimize communication barriers
level_5: Identifies complex barriers to effective communication
Effectively establishes and sustains therapeutic relationships, with attention to the patient’s/patient’s family’s concerns and context, regardless of complexity
Models shared decision making in communication with the patient/patient’s family, including in situations with a high degree of uncertainty/conflict

level_1: Uses language that values all members of the health care team
Communicates concerns and provides feedback to peers and learners
level_2: Recognizes the need for ongoing feedback with the health care team
Coordinates recommendations from different members of the health care team to optimize patient care
level_3: Communicates information effectively with all health care team members
Respectfully communicates feedback and constructive criticism to peers and superiors
level_4: Solicits feedback on performance as a member of the health care team
Models flexible communication strategies that value input from all health care team members, resolving conflict when needed
level_5: Uses active listening to adapt one’s communication style to fit team needs
Facilitates regular health care team-based feedback in complex situations

level_1: Accurately records information and communicates verbally with the rest of the health care team
Uses appropriate channels to offer clear and constructive suggestions to improve the system
level_2: Communicates about administrative issues through appropriate channels, as required by institutional policy
Communicates clearly and concisely, in an organized written form, and through verbal communication, including providing anticipatory guidance to others
level_3: Demonstrates organized diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning through notes and verbal communication
Initiates difficult conversations with appropriate stakeholders to improve the system
level_4: Respectfully communicates concerns about the system
Contributes to departmental or organizational initiatives to improve communication systems
level_5: Concisely and appropriately reports diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning in the patient record and through verbal communication
Facilitates dialogue regarding systems issues among larger community stakeholders
